summary: Alaka Chudal is an Indologist and linguist who completed a PhD at the University of Vienna (2009–2014). She served as a lecturer at Nepal Sanskrit University (1995–2007) and held a post at the University of Vienna in 2007.

Alan Avdagić works in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Jena (BA 2019–2023), the University of Würzburg (MA 2023–2025), and Free University of Berlin (attested 2026), holding a post at Würzburg.
Alan Butterworth (1864–1937) was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He was educated at Elizabeth College and studied at Balliol College, Oxford, in 1883.

Alan Coates Bouquet (1884–1976) worked in religious studies and Indology. Educated at St Dunstan's College, UCL, Trinity College, Cambridge (BA ~1902–1905), and Jesus College, Cambridge, he served as lecturer in history and comparative study of religion at Cambridge (1924–1955).

Alan Entwistle (1949–1996) specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Southampton and SOAS under J. C. Wright (PhD ~1982) and Jacob Ensink. He held posts at Groningen (1980–1985) and the University of Washington (appointed assistant professor 1986, associate professor 1990).

Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, sinology, and religious studies. He earned a BA at Johns Hopkins (1973–1977) and a PhD at Temple University (1980–1988), before holding professor and associate professor positions at the University of Delaware between 1990 and 2014.

Alan Gerard Wagner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2008) under Parimal G. Patil, also studying under Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.
Alan Gowans (1923–2001) was an art historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Toronto (1946) and Princeton University (1948, 1950).

Alan John Bayard Wace (1879–1957) was an archaeologist educated at Shrewsbury School and Pembroke College under Robert Alexander Neil. He held posts at the British School at Athens (1914–1923), Victoria and Albert Museum (1924–1934), Cambridge (1934–1944), and Alexandria University (1943–1952).

Alan Lomax (1915–2002) studied at Choate Rosemary Hall (~1929–1930), Harvard University (~1931–1932), the University of Texas at Austin (~1933–1936), Columbia University, and St. Mark's School of Texas.
Alan Nussbaum (born 1947) is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Harvard University (~1969–1976) and became a professor at Cornell University in 1985.

Alan Sponberg (1944–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD from the University of British Columbia. He served as a professor at Princeton (attested 1980–1987) and taught religious studies at Stanford (attested 1988).

Alan Watts (1915–1973) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After seminary studies, he held posts at Northwestern University (1944–1950), the American Academy of Asian Studies (1951–1957), Harvard (1962–1964), San Jose State (1968), and the Esalen Institute (~1962–1973).

Alasdair MacIntyre (1929–2025) was a philosopher who studied at Queen Mary and Manchester. He held appointments at Essex (~1966–1970), Brandeis (~1970–1972), Notre Dame (~1989–2010), Duke (~1995–2000), and London Metropolitan University (~2010).

Alasdair Urquhart (born 1945) is a philosopher who studied at Edinburgh (MA ~1963–1967) and Pittsburgh (PhD ~1967–1973). He was an assistant professor at University of Toronto Mississauga (1973–1975) and became Emeritus Professor at the University of Toronto in 1986.

Alastair Gornall is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who earned a PhD at Cambridge (2009–2013). He became Assistant Professor at Singapore University of Technology and Design in 2016, PTS Council Member, and SOAS Research Associate.
Albert Benjamin Norton (1847–1923) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Northwestern University (~1867–1871) and at Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary.

Albert Cuny (1869–1947) was a linguist who earned his PhD at the Sorbonne (~1896–1907), studying under Meillet, Henry, and Lévi. He taught at Lycée Edmond Perrier, Paris, and Bordeaux, where he was professor from 1910 to 1937.

Albert Debrunner (1884–1958) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Basel (1902–1907). He held professorial posts at Zurich (1917), Greifswald (1918), Jena (1925–1935), Bern (1920, 1935–1954), and taught at Basel (1940–1949).

Albert Esser (1885–1972) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He earned a Dr.med. at Heidelberg (~1907–1909) and a PhD at Cologne (1926–1930) under Willibald Kirfel, later serving as PD at Heidelberg (1940) and professor at Düsseldorf (1946–1961).
